newsitem.title: USA: Sun City in preliminary merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Sun City in preliminary merger talks.

text.p: Sun City Industries Inc said Friday it has entered into preliminary merger talks with a privately owned Miami-based specialty seafood producer and distributor, SeaSpecialties Inc.

If the discussed merger should be consummated, Sun City said, SeaSpecialties chief executive Harvey Oxenberg, in a stock-for-stock transaction, would own a majority of the stock and SeaSpecialties would assume control of the new company.
Thursday Sun City, a food distributor, reported continuing losses and said its auditors questioned the company's ability to continue as a going operation.
Sun City said the American Stock Exchange expects to resume trading in the company's stock following dissemination of the announcement about the SeaSpecialties talks.
It said the merger would create a food processing and distribution entity with sales of over $100 million per year.
Although a definitive merger agreement has yet to be signed, both Oxenberg and Sun City chief executive Malvin Avchen have indicated that discussions are progressing, the company said.
Any transaction will be subject to approval of the shareholders of both companies and holders of the Sun City's convertible bonds. It is anticipated the merger will close this summer, Sun City said.

Founded in 1954, SeaSpecialties is comprised of Florida Smoked Fish in Miami, Barnacle Seafood in Ft. Lauderdale, and Casa Mar SeaSpecialties on the Florida Keys. These divisions are wholesale producers of smoked, pickled, fresh and frozen seafood products in Florida.
